title: The turning qiblah
hookLine: at the mosque of the two qiblahs, the prayer turns mid-way from Jerusalem to Mecca (2:144)

cards: A row of people bowed in prayer, and a voice at the door. Bukhari tells it like this.
A man who has just prayed with the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, walks past another mosque where people are in the middle of their prayer, bent over, facing toward Jerusalem.
He calls out: I bear witness that I have just prayed with the Messenger of Allah facing Mecca. And they turn. Right there, in the middle of the prayer, as they are.

teach.b: The qiblah is the direction Muslims face in prayer. In Medina, the early Muslims had been praying toward Jerusalem.
Bukhari says the Prophet loved that his qiblah would be the Ka'bah in Mecca, the house tradition says Abraham raised.
And the Qur'an, in surah two, speaks of the turning of his face toward heaven, as if waiting. Then the verse comes.

In Pickthall's words, in surah two, verse one hundred forty-four: "So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship." The same verse says the believers too, wherever they are, are to turn their faces toward it.
Now go back to that mosque. The news arrives mid-prayer. Nobody holds a meeting.

Nobody says, let's finish this one the old way and start fresh tomorrow. They turn, in the rows, as they are. Bukhari has a second report of the people of Quba hearing it at the dawn prayer and doing the same.
Tradition remembers one of these places as the mosque of the two qiblahs, where a single prayer was offered facing two directions. And the prayer's first half wasn't wrong.
It was prayed in obedience, facing where they'd been told. The second half was too. What made both halves one prayer wasn't the direction.
It was the turning: being ready to change where you face the moment the call comes, without leaving the prayer.

how: Muslims face the Ka'bah in Mecca for every prayer, wherever they are, and a mosque's niche (mihrab) marks the qiblah; in Medina, visitors pray at the mosque known as the mosque of the two qiblahs.

games.q: you're bowed in prayer, facing Jerusalem. a man at the door calls out that the qiblah is now Mecca. what do you do?

games.why: in Bukhari they turned where they stood, in the middle of the prayer, and carried on.

practice: If you know where Mecca lies from where you're sitting, turn gently toward it now; if you don't, simply choose one direction and face it on purpose, and notice that your whole body is pointed somewhere.
Then think of one thing you've been facing out of habit, and ask, without throwing away what came before, whether it's time to turn. If you pray, you can ask Allah to keep your face toward Him.

wordCard.voice: Qiblah. The direction of prayer that changed from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah in Mecca, and worshipers turned toward it in the middle of their prayer. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'the qiblah', the direction Muslims face in prayer.

carryVoice: Your line: turn to the house. One prayer, two directions, and neither half wasted. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship
